# Padring Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The padring module is the chip-level pad ring front end. It instantiates the bidirectional pad cells, connects the functional pad-side signals to the internal logic-side signals, and applies the configured pad attributes and pad types.

The module has no functional state or history. Its observable behavior is a combinational function of the current input values and the static configuration:

- pad count and pad types,
- pad-to-bank assignment,
- scan roles,
- whether physical pad cells are present,
- the fixed set of shared dedicated/muxed pad pairs,
- the current mode-select values for those shared pairs.

## 2. Configuration

The padring is configured at build time with the following properties:

- The number of dedicated pads and the number of muxed pads.
- The pad type of every dedicated pad and every muxed pad, such as input-only, standard bidirectional, or open-drain bidirectional.
- The number of IO banks.
- The IO bank to which every dedicated pad and every muxed pad belongs.
- The scan role of every dedicated pad and every muxed pad.
- A build-time option that selects whether physical pad cells are instantiated.

The behavior described below applies to every configured pad unless explicitly stated otherwise.

## 3. Pad I/O Behavior

Each pad is a bidirectional physical pad wire. For each pad, the module provides:

- an output data value,
- an output enable value,
- an input data observation,
- a raw input data observation,
- a pad attribute field.

### 3.1 Output Driving

The output enable controls the pad driver:

- When the output enable is asserted, the pad must be driven with the output data value, subject to the pad type and pad attributes.
- When the output enable is deasserted, the pad must be high-impedance and must not drive the pad wire.

The pad type determines which pad-cell variant is used. The padring does not override the pad type; it instantiates the intended pad behavior for each configured type.

### 3.2 Input Observation

The padring always activates the input path of every pad. A pad may still be input-disabled if the corresponding input-disable attribute is set, but the padring itself does not dynamically disable pad inputs.

For every pad, the module provides two input observations:

- The normal input observation reflects the pad, including the configured input/output inversion attribute.
- The raw input observation reflects the same pad value without the inversion attribute.

The raw observation is available independently of the normal observation and is intended for infrastructure and DFT uses.

### 3.3 Pad Attributes

The following pad attributes are received per pad and passed through to the pad cell:

- input/output inversion,
- virtual open-drain enable,
- pull enable,
- pull select,
- keeper enable,
- Schmitt trigger enable,
- open-drain enable,
- input disable,
- slew rate,
- drive strength.

The padring must not alter, ignore, or reinterpret these attributes. The pad cell is responsible for applying them.

## 4. Dedicated and Muxed Pads

There are two pad categories:

- Dedicated pads have fixed functional connections.
- Muxed pads are intended to be routed through the pinmux matrix.

Except for the fixed shared pairs described below, every dedicated pad and every muxed pad behaves independently:

- The dedicated pad is driven from its own dedicated output data and output enable.
- The dedicated input observations are taken from the dedicated pad.
- The muxed pad is driven from its own muxed output data and output enable.
- The muxed input observations are taken from the muxed pad.

## 5. Shared IOB Pad Pairs

Four fixed pairs exist between certain dedicated SPI data pads and the first four muxed pads of the B group:

1. Dedicated SPI host data pad 2 with muxed pad IOB0.
2. Dedicated SPI host data pad 3 with muxed pad IOB1.
3. Dedicated SPI device data pad 2 with muxed pad IOB2.
4. Dedicated SPI device data pad 3 with muxed pad IOB3.

Each pair has an independent mode select. The four mode selects do not affect one another.

### 5.1 Normal Mode

When the pair’s mode select is deasserted:

- The dedicated pad is driven by its own dedicated output data and output enable.
- The muxed pad is driven by its own muxed output data and output enable.
- The dedicated input observations are taken from the dedicated pad.
- The muxed input observations are taken from the muxed pad.

### 5.2 Shared Mode

When the pair’s mode select is asserted:

- The dedicated pad output is driven from the muxed pad’s output data and output enable instead of the dedicated output path.
- The muxed pad output remains driven from its own muxed output data and output enable.
- The dedicated input observations are still taken from the dedicated pad.
- The muxed input observations are taken from the dedicated pad instead of from the muxed pad.

In shared mode, both pads therefore share the same output driver state, while the muxed-side input path observes the dedicated pad.

## 6. Scan Support

The padring accepts a scan clock and a multi-bit scan mode request.

The scan mode request is redundantly encoded and is decoded to a single active enable before being distributed to the pad cells.

Each pad has a configured scan role:

- no scan role,
- scan input role,
- scan output role.

When scan mode is active:

- Pads configured with a scan input role behave as scan input pads.
- Pads configured with a scan output role behave as scan output pads.
- Pads with no scan role continue to follow their normal functional behavior.

The scan mode selection applies to the pad cell behavior and is independent from the shared-pair mode selection.

## 7. Bank Power Status

The padring maintains one power status per IO bank.

When physical pad cells are instantiated, the power status values are sourced from the physical pad layer. When physical pad cells are not instantiated, all bank power status values are tied to the inactive state.

Every pad receives the power status of the IO bank to which it is assigned. The padring does not otherwise interpret power statuses. A pad whose bank power status is inactive is subject to the pad technology’s power-sequencing behavior, which may include disabled output drivers or high-impedance pad behavior.
